correctness.rationale: Every profile's value must lie in the unique joint cell for its action blocks. For a doubleton, a fixed copy must see both symbols in its slice of that cell; partitions ensure that profiles outside that cell cannot supply either symbol. If fewer than two axes have length at least two, fixing the only potentially varying axis leaves a one-entry slice. If two axes vary, parity of their copy indices supplies both outcomes in every fixed-action slice, even for budgets greater than two. Singleton cells use their only outcome and impose no constraint. The cell constructions glue because joint cells partition the outcome set and all type triples are allowed. Each triangle needs two doubled vertices exactly when every one of its edges is covered. Extra copies beyond two are removable without violating feasibility, and isolated vertices need only one. Thus all optimum vectors correspond exactly to minimum covers and the displayed example has total 8. Independently tested 38 small cell shapes with bitmask slice-surjectivity enumeration, not the parity construction (`python3 /workspace/frozen_review_replay.py 4`); this is bounded corroboration. The frozen script was read, not run.
